headline: A real button with pseudo-states, a media query and a variant conditional folds completely on both yak compilers, and on Solid that puts `@yak/solid` level with hand-written Solid at 1.68M renders/s.

microbench.why: Everything in this button resolves at build time — the responsive flip, the four pseudo-states, the WCAG pseudo-element, the variant conditional — so `yak-solid` books 0.014 ms of lib self-time and reaches 1.68M renders/s, within 4% of `vanilla-solid`'s 1.74M and nearly twice `next-yak`'s 894,000. The React lanes are held back by react-dom itself: `next-yak` spends 1.61 ms of its 1.98 ms there. `styled-components` at 193,000 and `emotion` at 145,000 serialize the whole state matrix per instance, and `panda-props` at 103,000 resolves style props for it.

autocannon.why: `yak-solid` at 880 req/s and `vanilla-solid` at 816 lead by rendering less framework per element; `next-yak` holds 599 with `next-yak-css` at 602. `emotion` serves 132 req/s, serializing five pseudo-state blocks inside every request.

attribution.why: `vanilla-solid` renders in 0.941 ms and `yak-solid` in 0.992 ms with 0.014 ms of lib — the compiler leaves nothing behind. `next-yak-css` at 1.39 ms and `next-yak` at 1.98 ms are mostly react-dom. The contrast is `next-yak-nofold` at 2.65 ms with 1.45 ms of lib, which is what this button costs when the wrapper survives, and `emotion` at 8.38 ms with 5.90 ms of its own runtime.

hydrate.why: `vanilla-solid` at 56.0 ms, `bamboo` at 58.2 ms and `next-yak-css` at 58.7 ms lead a narrow field where the ordering is framework noise. `styled-components` at 165 ms and `goober` at 162 ms are the separations worth naming.

inp.why: Eleven lanes answer between 6.5 ms and 7.7 ms, flat given the spread, with `cn` at 6.5 ms nominally first. The Solid lanes read 20.8 ms and 23.4 ms here, and that is the measurement's asymmetry rather than a Solid weakness: the React pass re-renders with an unchanged variant and writes nothing, while the Solid pass flips variant, disabled and icon on every instance and updates the DOM. `emotion` at 31.4 ms and `panda-props` at 26.2 ms are slow on their own account.

mount.why: `vanilla-solid` at 40.1 ms and `yak-solid` at 41.9 ms mount roughly three times faster than the React field, which starts at 111 ms. With the CSS fully extracted the mount is DOM construction; `emotion` at 185 ms injects its sheet before the first paint.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, near 0.37 ms — higher than the toy cases because each button carries a pseudo-element and a media query, but identical across lanes since they all end at the same class list.

payload.why: The next-yak css-prop lanes lead at roughly 4,300 gz B. `yak-solid` reaches 13,948 B, and 9,724 B of that is HTML: this DOM has nine elements per button, so Solid's per-element hydration key is charged nine times over where `next-yak` ships 3,308 B for the same markup. `cn` at 23,804 B is the heaviest lane in the case, 13,054 B of it library JS.

nsweep.why: `yak-solid` at 2.21 ms and `vanilla-solid` at 2.45 ms hold the flattest lines at 4,000 instances, against 4.77 ms for `next-yak` and 39.7 ms for `panda-props`. A fully folded button has no per-instance styling work left to scale.
